items.title: Barry Kernfeld interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 16, 2020
items.q: Joe Zawinul — well I’m sorry, except for “Birdland” he just bores me to tears. ... But I don’t think that that handicaps very much writing a Zawinul Grove article.

ctx.x: Well I don’t have to ask that question now. Sometimes I do ask that question, of time travel, but you just took care of it already. So in your role as an editor you’ve done so much of it. I wonder if it’s sometimes hard for you if there’s an artist that really demands attention and of course should be included whether it’s the book or the on-line edition, but you don’t particularly care for their music. Do you recognize that you might need to hand this off to somebody else or does it affect the way you think…

I like to think that it would affect it only in a small way. There are things like that, it does happen. If I can hand it off I will, sure I’d be happy to have someone do it who is a complete enthusiast for it. But I think that is much less of a problem for Grove, where we’re so concerned with the nitty gritty biographical and discographical and videographical details and bibliographical details, and not with say writing a book about them or writing a review of their record, which is a different kind of writing…
Okay. Does the fact that the next thing’s going to be an on-line edition, you literally don’t have to worry about how heavy it’s going to be, how many pages you’re creating?
